biography.plain_text: Nelson Piquet is a Brazilian former racing driver who won three Formula One world championships and 23 Grands Prix. After retiring, he founded Autotrac, a Brasília-based telematics company serving transport and logistics operators. The technology business ultimately earned him more than his racing career, and he remains chairman of its board.

long_biography.plain_text:
Nelson Piquet's engineering instincts shaped a Formula One career built on technical feedback and race strategy. With Brabham, he became the first driver to win the championship with a turbocharged engine, then added another title for Williams. His work with designers and mechanics made car development as central to his reputation as outright speed.

Piquet applied the same practical focus to freight technology after returning to Brazil. Autotrac introduced satellite-based fleet tracking to transport operators that often had little experience with computerised logistics. He led the company as it developed equipment, software and mobile-data services around monitoring and risk management. He remained its board chairman in 2025.

His legal name is Nelson Piquet Souto Maior, but Brazilian surname structure does not map cleanly to filling the blank middle-names field without duplicating or altering the established public name, so no name-field proposal is made.

[2] Autotrac: Autotrac is the Brazilian fleet-tracking and logistics-technology company Piquet founded and still chairs. [4] Fleet telematics: Autotrac develops equipment, software and mobile-data services for vehicle and freight monitoring. [5] Formula One Grand Prix winner: Piquet won 23 Formula One Grands Prix. [7] Race-car development driver: Piquet was noted for technical feedback, extensive testing and development of the Brabham-BMW turbo car. [8] Satellite navigation: Piquet commercialised satellite-based vehicle tracking and navigation technology in Brazil through Autotrac. [9] Supply-chain technology: Autotrac provides monitoring, communications and risk-management technology for freight and logistics operators. [10] Technology entrepreneur: After Formula One, Piquet founded and built Autotrac into a major fleet-tracking technology company. [11] Williams Racing: Williams was the Formula One team with which Piquet won his third world championship. [12] World champion: Piquet won the Formula One drivers' world championship three times.
